topic.title: Suggesting Changes to a Project
topic.shortdesc: Contributors propose their changes to a project by creating a review task from the changes in their personal workspace.

body.p: Instead of committing changes directly to the project, Contributors submits their changes to the project team. The project maintainers and owners then review the changes to decide whether to integrate them into the project.

section.title: Proposing Your Changes
section.p: To suggest changes to a project:

ol.li: Open the project and edit the files you want to change in your personal workspace.
Select the Changes view in the left stripe to view the files you modified.
A review task will be created from the complete set of changes in your workspace.
Click Submit for Approval.Deleted and renamed files cannot be sent for review. If your changes include any, revert them before submitting.

In the resulting Submit Changes for Approval dialog box, enter a title for the task.
Optionally, enter a Description, specify a Due Date, or select a Context Publication so that the files are rendered as a hierarchical tree. There is also an Include all project files as context option that specifies whether project files are included in the task to provide context for reviewers and prevent missing images or broken links.
Click the Submit for Approval button to submit your changes.

section.p: Result: The review task is created and the project maintainers are notified of your submission. The task is created without an owner and waits for a project maintainer or owner to take ownership of the task. Once they do, you will receive an email notification. For details, see After You Suggest Changes.

ul.li: Keep each proposal focused on a single subject. Because the task includes every change in your workspace, unrelated edits are included in the same review.
Give the task a title that explains what you changed and why, so the project team can understand the proposal before opening it.
Use the task description to provide any information reviewers need, such as the source of information you corrected.
